study.research_problem: Major acetabular bone loss in revision THA requires immediate structural support and restoration of bone stock, but advanced porous-metal/cup-cage constructs may be inaccessible in resource-limited systems.
study.exact_gap: The short- to mid-term performance and failure conditions of defect-shaped structural allograft blocks fixed with screws and supporting a cemented cup remain uncertain, especially for severe Paprosky type 3 defects (S001:C01-S002:C02).
study.objective_or_hypothesis: Describe clinical and radiographic outcomes of structural homologous block allograft plus a cemented acetabular component in 13 consecutive major acetabular revisions (S001:C01-S003:C01).
study.study_design: Level-IV retrospective case series of 13 hips revised from 2016-2021, with standardized radiographs, final HHS, predefined radiographic failure, Kaplan-Meier survival, and exploratory graft-origin log-rank analysis (S003:C01; S007:C01-S008:C01).
study.sample_or_model: Thirteen heterogeneous Paprosky 2B, 2C, 3A, or 3B defects; structural graft source depended on bone-bank availability, and every case also underwent an individualized femoral revision (S003:C01-S004:C02).
comparators: No concurrent modern porous-metal, cup-cage, or other reconstruction control
Preoperative versus final HHS within the same patients
Exploratory femoral-condyle versus other graft-source survival comparison with only two failures
Failure versus nonfailure case interpretation across different defect severities
method_spine: Classify acetabular defect and select available structural allograft.
Shape graft to defect, screw it to ilium, add morselized interface graft, ream the construct, and cement a cup through host-graft containment purchase.
Use partial weight bearing for six weeks and scheduled radiographic/clinical follow-up.
Define migration/radiolucency failure a priori and report HHS with uncertainty.
Analyze failures as mechanism-generating cases while limiting subgroup inference.
Frame value relative to resource constraints rather than untested superiority.

verification: Five to six intraoperative cultures per case were negative, and follow-up/rehabilitation schedules and radiographic failure thresholds were prespecified (S006:C01-S007:C01).
One specialized surgeon, blinded to final HHS, assessed graft incorporation/migration; no inter-observer reliability or advanced migration measurement was available (S007:C01).
validation: Observed radiographic consolidation, absence of loosening, and HHS improvement in 11 cases support short- to mid-term clinical feasibility, not mechanical validation of graft strength or comparative effectiveness (S009:C01-S013:C01).
Conventional radiographs cannot validate subtle micromotion, actual graft revascularization, bone-stock restoration, or load sharing.
sensitivity: The authors examine defect severity and graft source descriptively, but only two failures make log-rank/subgroup findings unstable and highly confounded (S010:C01-S011:C01; S014:C03-S014:C05).
No sensitivity analysis varies failure definition, censoring, imaging interpretation, graft coverage, screw pattern, cup position, or weight-bearing protocol.
application_prediction: Use as a lower-cost reconstruction and as a bridge to future revision is an application rationale; durability beyond the observed follow-up and equivalence to modern constructs are unknown (S014:C04-S015:C01).

primary_outcomes: Mean follow-up was about 54 months; 11 of 13 cases showed radiographic consolidation without defined failure, while two severe defects failed early at seven and nine months through graft fragmentation and cup migration (S009:C01-S012:C01).
Five-year construct survival was estimated at 84% with a very wide 95% CI of approximately 55-95%, reflecting only two events (S011:C01).

Mean HHS increased from 34.5 to 70.1, an average improvement of 35.6 points (95% CI 28.1-43.2); without a control, improvement cannot be assigned solely to the acetabular technique (S009:C01; S013:C01).

Both failures used femoral-condyle grafts, but also occurred in Paprosky 3A/3B high-instability defects; the apparent graft-origin association is hypothesis-generating and vulnerable to Type-I error/confounding (S010:C01-S011:C01; S014:C03-S014:C05).
study.highest_evidence_level_reached: Small uncontrolled short- to mid-term clinical case series with documented early mechanical failures and broad survival uncertainty; no comparative, long-term, or direct mechanical evidence.

argument_map.central_claim: Defect-shaped structural allograft plus a cemented cup can provide a practical medium-term reconstruction for selected major acetabular defects where advanced implants are unavailable, but severe type-3 defects showed early mechanical failure and the series cannot establish durability, comparative value, or graft-source effects.
data: Thirteen consecutive reconstructions with defect/graft/technique details, serial conventional radiographs, HHS, two early failures, and wide-CI survival (S003:C01-S013:C01).
Failure-case descriptions linking severe defect instability, graft fragmentation, and migration (S010:C01-S014:C03).
argument_map.warrant: Clinical function plus maintained component position and radiographic graft consolidation are consistent with feasibility, while fragmentation/migration in high-demand defects exposes a structural-support boundary requiring dedicated testing and comparison.
backing: The paper contextualizes allograft as an accessible bone-stock option and modern reinforcement constructs as costly/unavailable in its health system (S002:C01-S002:C02; S014:C01).
argument_map.qualifier: Selected-case, resource-contextual, short- to mid-term feasibility.
rebuttals_or_boundaries: No control group distinguishes the technique from other revision constructs or natural postoperative recovery.
Only two failures make Kaplan-Meier and log-rank subgroup estimates extremely imprecise (S011:C01; S014:C03-S014:C05).
Defect severity, pelvic discontinuity, graft origin, graft geometry, coverage, fixation, and patient factors are confounded.
All patients also had femoral revision, contributing to HHS and complications.
Conventional radiography and single-reader assessment cannot detect subtle migration or verify biological incorporation.
Mean 54 months is shorter than the reported 6-10-year window in which structural allograft failures may rise (S014:C04).

measured: Defect class, graft source, technique, cultures, rehabilitation, serial radiographs, migration/radiolucency, graft fragmentation, HHS, follow-up, and re-revision status (S003:C01-S013:C01).
inferred: Restored bone stock, future-revision facilitation, load sharing, initial mechanical resistance, and protection during incorporation are plausible rationales not directly quantified (S002:C02; S014:C01-S014:C04).

The authors attribute failure mainly to severe structural deficiency and infer that reinforcement rings/cup-cage constructs are mandatory, but only two uncontrolled failures support this claim (S014:C02-S014:C03).
recommended: Prospective multicenter comparisons, defect-stratified cohorts, CT/radiostereometric migration, mechanical testing/modeling, longer than ten-year follow-up, and transparent cost/resource analysis are needed (S014:C04-S015:C01).
proxy_to_outcome_bridges: Conventional radiographic density/consolidation is not histological incorporation, revascularization, or restored mechanical bone stock.
HHS improvement is a whole-patient functional outcome affected by acetabular and femoral revision, rehabilitation, and baseline severity.
Two early failures can reveal a failure mode but cannot estimate a stable subgroup effect or prove graft-source causality.
Five-year survival with a 55-95% CI is too imprecise for strong comparative claims.
Resource accessibility is an implementation advantage, not evidence of biomechanical equivalence.
overclaim_risks: The discussion says type-3 failures confirm that constrained load-sharing implants are mandatory and consistently superior, stronger than this uncontrolled series permits (S014:C02-S014:C03).
A log-rank P value of 0.04 with two events can be overread unless event count, CI, confounding, and Type-I-error warning accompany it (S011:C01-S012:C01; S014:C03-S014:C05).
The automatic case-report, porous/lattice, and animal cues are incorrect; this is a 13-patient clinical case series without a porous-device experiment.

section_moves.move: Connect defect classification to a reproducible reconstruction chain
section_moves.execution: The paper describes graft source/availability, defect shaping, screw fixation, interface morselized graft, reaming, containment hole, cement pressurization, cup implantation, and rehabilitation (S003:C01-S007:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: For complex reconstructions, write anatomy/defect class, biological material, mechanical fixation, interface preparation, load progression, and failure definition as one method spine.
section_moves.failure_mode: Technical completeness does not substitute for a comparator or direct mechanical validation.

section_moves.execution: The two failures are described by timing, defect class, fragmentation, migration, infection status, and lack of re-revision rather than being hidden in a success percentage (S010:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: In small implant series, report every failure as anatomy/configuration, time, observation, plausible mechanism, alternative explanation, and subsequent management.
section_moves.failure_mode: A failure narrative can generate mechanisms but not prove them.

section_moves.move: Report survival with event count and confidence interval
section_moves.execution: The series reports 84% five-year survival with a broad 95% CI and explicitly notes only two events (S011:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Always place Kaplan-Meier estimate, CI, number at risk/events, censoring, and follow-up distribution together; avoid subgroup inference when events are sparse.
section_moves.failure_mode: A nominal subgroup P value cannot overcome two-event instability.

section_moves.move: Use resource context as a separate decision axis
section_moves.execution: The paper contrasts accessible certified bone-bank grafts with unavailable high-cost porous-metal/cup-cage systems and frames the technique as a pragmatic option (S014:C01-S014:C05).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Discuss effectiveness, failure boundary, resource availability, and future revision value as separate axes rather than treating affordability as efficacy.
section_moves.failure_mode: Implementation necessity does not prove equal durability.

section_moves.move: Turn subgroup association into a bounded hypothesis
section_moves.execution: Although both failures used femoral-condyle grafts and log-rank P was 0.04, the authors repeatedly flag two-event confounding and Type-I error (S011:C01; S014:C03-S014:C05).
section_moves.transferable_principle: For sparse-event exploratory subgroups, state event count, competing explanation, uncertainty, and the exact prospective comparison needed; use hypothesis language.
section_moves.failure_mode: Do not rank graft sources or prescribe constructs from a nominal P value.

author_reported: Retrospective design, 13 heterogeneous cases, short follow-up, two failures/low power and Type-I-error risk, variable graft source, no modern-device control, and conventional radiography only (S014:C04-S014:C05).
reader_identified: No sample-size rationale, prospective protocol, standardized CT/RSA, inter-rater reliability, or independent outcome assessment.
HHS before-after improvement is confounded by femoral revision, rehabilitation, selection, and survivorship.
No direct measurement of load transfer, graft strength, fixation micromotion, biological incorporation, or restored bone stock.
Paprosky severity and pelvic discontinuity confound graft-source and failure interpretations.
Kaplan-Meier estimates and log-rank P values are unstable with only two events and very small risk sets.
No comparative cost-effectiveness, patient-reported quality of life, or long-term re-revision outcome.
Four-to-five-year averages may precede the main late failure window.
likely_bias_direction: Survivor and selection bias likely inflate feasibility and functional outcomes.
Retrospective salience of the two failures may overstate a single mechanical explanation or the need for a specific reinforcement construct.
Resource-context advocacy may favor benefit interpretation despite absent comparator.
limitations.scope_boundary: The series documents an accessible reconstruction's medium-term course and a severe-defect failure signal; it does not establish comparative durability, graft-source effects, biological incorporation, or a universal type-3 fixation mandate.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Write complex reconstruction Methods as defect classification to graft/device configuration to interface/fixation to rehabilitation to failure definition.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Clinical Methods, device configuration table, and reproducibility figure.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Defect-shaped grafting is patient-adapted surgery, not digitally validated patient-specific implant engineering.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Treat every implant failure as a mechanism-generating case with configuration, timing, observation, competing mechanisms, and management.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Results failure table and Discussion mechanism paragraph.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Two failures identify a warning signal but do not prove a universal mechanism or treatment rule.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Write sparse-event survival/subgroup results with event count, CI, confounding, Type-I-error risk, and hypothesis-only language.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Statistical Results, subgroup paragraph, and limitations.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: A log-rank P value from two failures is not a reliable graft-source effect.

critical_weaknesses: Thirteen uncontrolled heterogeneous cases and only two failures.
Conventional radiography/single assessor and no direct mechanical or biological incorporation measures.
Short follow-up relative to late allograft failure and unstable subgroup statistics.

summary_zh: 这不是单病例、动物或多孔支架研究，而是 13 例翻修髋臼的回顾性病例系列。结构性同种异体骨块按 Paprosky 缺损塑形、螺钉固定、界面加颗粒骨并承托骨水泥杯；11 例在平均约 54 个月时影像稳定，2 例严重 3A/3B 缺损在 7/9 个月出现骨块碎裂和杯迁移。5 年生存 84%，但 95% CI 约 55–95%，只有两个事件。两例均用股骨髁移植物且 log-rank P=0.04，但缺损严重度和骨盆连续性严重混杂，因此只能生成假设。论文最值得蒸馏的是把失败当成主证据：配置—时间—失效观察—竞争机制—处置；同时任何稀疏事件生存/亚组结果都必须同报事件数、CI、混杂和 I 类错误。资源可及性应作为独立决策轴，不能代替机械等效或长期耐久证据。
reader_notes: Primary Codex reader reviewed every non-reference packet section, including the full patient table, technique, radiographic criteria, both failures, survival/HHS analyses, and resource-context discussion.
The automatic case-report, porous/lattice, and animal cues are incorrect.
The paper is a strong failure-analysis and sparse-event reporting exemplar, not a comparative device-efficacy study.
